target_customer: Supermarket and grocery retailers that pay monthly for robots that restock shelves at night and pick e-grocery orders by day
problem: Restocking shelves and picking online grocery orders is repetitive store labor. Retailers have no single robot that does both inside existing aisles without a retrofit.
business_model: Robots-as-a-service sold monthly to retailers, using off-the-shelf wheeled humanoids plus the company's own operating system and AI models
product_category: Retail humanoid robotics and physical AI

founders.name: Samarth Malhotra
previous_startups: Jumps Tronic (hardware manufacturing, outcome not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he scaled Parts World USA from under $100k to $3M revenue over four years.

founders.name: Kristof Floch
education: ETH Zurich, Robotics, Systems and Control (Excellence Scholar)
founders.background_notes: Research on learning-based control with first-author papers per YC page.

founders.name: Adam Weinhardt-Kovacs
founders.background_notes: Led a pick-and-place deployment at live sorting centers at Flink Robotics per YC page.

competitors.name: HIVE Robots
competitors.what: Unitree G1 humanoids trained in a Danish foetex supermarket for overnight shelf restocking, sold as hourly robotics as a service
competitors.traction_then: Trial with human operators guiding movements, aiming for independent restocking by early 2027

competitors.name: Telexistence
competitors.what: Robots that fill shelves at Japanese convenience stores
competitors.traction_then: FamilyMart and Lawson trialing robots as shelf fillers

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable manipulation in cluttered retail aisles with off-the-shelf hardware needs learned policies, perception and safe operation around people. Two robots reportedly run in two stores, but the figures are company claims.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware is off the shelf, so the edge rests on software and policy data that rivals in Denmark, Japan and China are also collecting. Early deployments could build switching costs but none are shown.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Unknown, the company is weeks old. Other humanoid firms were already trialing retail restocking in autumn 2026.

market_need_then: Retail restocking is labor intensive. A fourweekmba article frames a roughly $60B grocer restocking bill, a figure not independently checked. Danish and Japanese chains were piloting robots in 2026 and Walmart and Target were reported buying robots at record rates.

branding.domain_note: Uses theseus.bot, not theseus.com. Another YC company named Theseus (drone navigation) exists, and several unrelated Theseus robotics entities appear in search.

identity.logo: Not described by any source opened
identity.mascot_or_character: The robot is named Theo per press coverage
identity.visual_style: Plain site with a book a private preview call to action
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, with bold emphasis; tagline Humanoids for restocking, rotation and picking

brand_strength.rationale: Brand is new and only covered at launch. The Theseus name collides with another YC company and other robotics entities, so search confusion is visible already.

outcome_analysis: Theseus Robotics is active and only weeks past its launch in November 2026, so there is no outcome yet. The company claims two robots in two stores and pilots for up to ten more in 2027, but those figures come from its own posts. Funding beyond YC is not public, and a Dealroom entry of $125k is unverified and mismatched on founding year.
notes: Dealroom lists a $125k seed and a founding year of 2022 and describes warehouse AMRs, which conflicts with the YC page (founded 2026). Treated as unverified, not recorded as a round. The YC launch post was paywalled in the excerpt read. Jianwen Cao is named CRO in the launch post but is not on the YC founder list, so not recorded as a founder. Funding cross-check found no second source.
